Morning rules for the ramp team
This section explains the steps that matter

Companion Animal Travel Desk handling standards

This section guides the desk team in managing animal travel cases from booking review through arrival support. Staff must keep the passenger informed, confirm the animal is accepted for the route, and prepare the service record before handoff to the ramp team. When a rabbit is listed, <<FACT F064>>. The check-in review must confirm the crate is secure, clean, and large enough for safe posture, and staff must refuse transport if the container is damaged or unsuitable. The team also verifies that water, bedding, and identification are in place, and that the passenger understands the relief and pickup process.

If a passenger arrives with more than one animal, the desk should separate each case in the record and attach the correct labels without mixing documents. Staff must speak plainly, avoid promising exceptions, and escalate any concern about distress, noise, or escape risk to the senior coordinator at once. If the traveler asks for help, provide calm instructions and keep the exchange focused on the animal, the baggage path, and the next point of contact. The desk should note any special handling needs and pass them forward with the regular movement sheet.

Before release for flight, the agent confirms that the traveler has the required paperwork and that the crate remains sealed after inspection. After arrival, the desk follows the handoff record, verifies pickup by the named recipient, and closes the file only after the animal is accounted for. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty manager for any case that falls outside normal handling.
